title: Architecture Traceability Link Recovery
short_description: Evaluation of LLMs' capability to recover traceability links between software architecture documentation and source code using component name extraction
long_description: This benchmark evaluates the effectiveness of Large Language Models in recovering traceability links between Software Architecture Documentation (SAD) and source code. The approach leverages LLMs to extract component names as simple Software Architecture Models (SAMs) to bridge the semantic gap between documentation and code. Using the TransArC methodology, the benchmark tests whether LLM-extracted component names can enable transitive traceability link recovery without requiring manually created architecture models. The evaluation covers four distinct traceability scenarios: direct documentation-to-code linking, documentation-to-component model linking, component model-to-code linking, and transitive documentation-to-code linking with intermediate models.

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.description: The ratio of correctly identified trace links to the total number of identified trace links

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.description: The ratio of correctly identified trace links to the total number of actual trace links in the gold standard

metrics.name: F1-Score
metrics.description: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a balanced measure of traceability performance

metrics.name: Weighted Average F1
metrics.description: F1-score weighted by the number of expected trace links in the gold standard for each project
